title: Characterisation
description:
Everything measured during one characterisation run.

Written to disk at checkpoints throughout the procedure so that a run which
fails part-way still leaves its partial results behind.

Every measured field is an `Option`, `None` until it's measured, because the
file is saved before anything is — and a run that's quit part-way leaves the
rest as `null`.

cold_resistance.description:
Everything recorded while measuring the cold resistance, once its
setup has finished.

filament_id.description:
An identifier for the filament under test, entered by the operator.

`None` until then. It's the first thing the procedure asks for, before
any measurement is taken, so a file with a measurement in it always has
one — but a run quit at that first prompt is still saved, and `None`
(`null` in the file) says so honestly where an empty string wouldn't.

in_vacuum.description:
Whether the run was in a pumped-down chamber.

`false` for a bench test with `--no-vacuum`, e.g. against a precision
resistor standing in for a filament, which needs no vacuum. Recorded so
a results file always says which it was.

started_at.description: When the run started, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

ColdResistance.description:
Everything recorded while measuring the cold resistance.

Created once both temperatures are known and saved at every step after, so
the `Option` fields are exactly the ones not yet known at those saves, and
an aborted run still leaves everything measured up to that point on disk.

analysis.description: The fit and uncertainty budget, once every setpoint has been measured.

chamber_end_temperature_celsius.description:
The operator-entered chamber temperature at the filament's flange after
the setpoints, in °C, once they've all been measured.

chamber_start_temperature_celsius.description:
The operator-entered chamber temperature at the filament's flange
before the setpoints, in °C.

fit_parameters.description: Every scalar input to the fit, recorded when the fit runs.

points.description: One entry per setpoint, in the order measured.

positive_polarity.description:
The relay state that gave a positive voltage, once the vertical scale
has been chosen. Never `Nil`.

references.description:
The measurements at the reference current, interleaved with the
setpoints to track the mount's warming, in the order measured.

room_temperature_celsius.description:
The operator-entered room temperature near the supply in °C, for the
supply's accuracy band.

vertical_scale_volts_per_division.description:
The oscilloscope's vertical scale for every measurement, once it's been
chosen.

ColdResistanceAnalysis.description:
The fit and uncertainty budget: exactly the output of
`cold_resistance_fit.py`.

Every uncertainty is a standard uncertainty. Expanded uncertainties aren't
stored: they're twice these, and are computed for display.

chi_squared_p_value.description:
The probability of a chi-squared at least this large if the line and
the per-point uncertainties are right.

corrected_resistances_ohms.description:
Each point's resistance less the mount's drift since the first
reference, $R'_i$, with its full uncertainty, in the order of the
points. These are what's fitted.

current_gain_uncertainty_ohms.description: The contribution of the supply's readback gain error.

current_offset_uncertainty_ohms.description:
The contribution of the supply's readback offset error, from the corner
analysis.

drift_corrections_ohms.description:
The drift subtracted from each point, $\Delta R(t_i)$, with its
uncertainty, in the order of the points.

fit_uncertainty_ohms.description:
The statistical uncertainty of the fit's intercept, inflated by the
Birge ratio when that's above 1.

offset_corner_resistances_ohms.description:
The fitted intercept with the readback offset at its lower and upper
bounds, in that order.

reduced_chi_squared.description: Chi-squared divided by its degrees of freedom.

reference_drift_ohms.description:
The last reference's resistance less the first's: the mount's drift
over the run.

reference_resistance_ohms.description:
The cold resistance corrected to the reference temperature, $R_{20}$,
with its combined standard uncertainty.

resistance_ohms.description:
The cold resistance at the filament temperature, $R_0$: the fit's
intercept, with its combined standard uncertainty. The other
`*_uncertainty_ohms` fields are that uncertainty's components.

slope_ohms_per_amp_squared.description:
The fit's slope, $b$, which measures how strongly the filament heats
itself.

temperature_coefficient_uncertainty_ohms.description:
The contribution of the uncertainty in tungsten's temperature
coefficient to `reference_resistance_ohms`' uncertainty.

temperature_uncertainty_ohms.description:
The contribution of the uncertainty in the filament temperature to
`reference_resistance_ohms`' uncertainty.

voltage_gain_uncertainty_ohms.description: The contribution of the oscilloscope's gain error.

warnings.description: Warnings raised by the analysis, e.g. a poor fit.

ColdResistanceFitParameters.description:
The fit's scalar inputs.

With the points, this is everything `cold_resistance_fit.py` needs, so the
fit can be re-run from the results file alone, and anyone reading the file
can see which assumptions produced the result.

current_gain_bound.description:
The bound on the supply's current readback gain error, relative, after
widening for the room temperature.

current_offset_bound_amps.description:
The bound on the supply's current readback offset in amperes, after
widening for the room temperature.

filament_temperature_bound_kelvin.description:
The bound on the filament temperature in kelvin, $a_T$: the
thermometer's bound.

filament_temperature_celsius.description:
The filament temperature, $T_f$: the chamber temperature at the start,
since the references correct for any warming during the run.

reference_temperature_celsius.description: The temperature the resistance is corrected to.

temperature_coefficient_bound_per_kelvin.description: The bound on tungsten's temperature coefficient of resistance, $a_\alpha$.

temperature_coefficient_per_kelvin.description:
Tungsten's temperature coefficient of resistance near room
temperature, $\alpha$.

voltage_gain_bound.description: The bound on the oscilloscope's gain error, relative.

ColdResistancePoint.description:
The measurements at one setpoint or reference, filed by the sign of the
voltage rather than by relay state, so nothing downstream needs to know
which relay state is which.

analysis.description: The output of `cold_resistance_point.py`, once it's run.

first_polarity.description:
The relay state measured first. With `positive_polarity`, this says
which measurement came first and so which settle followed the ramp from
the previous setpoint. Never `Nil`.

negative_current_amps.description: The current in the polarity that gives a negative voltage.

negative_settle_seconds.description:
How long the filament took to settle in the polarity that gives a
negative voltage, in seconds.

negative_time_seconds.description:
The midpoint of the sampling window in the polarity that gives a
negative voltage, in seconds since the cold-resistance measurement
started.

negative_voltage_volts.description: The voltage in the polarity that gives a negative voltage.

positive_current_amps.description: The current in the polarity that gives a positive voltage.

positive_settle_seconds.description:
How long the filament took to settle in the polarity that gives a
positive voltage, in seconds.

positive_time_seconds.description:
The midpoint of the sampling window in the polarity that gives a
positive voltage, in seconds since the cold-resistance measurement
started.

positive_voltage_volts.description: The voltage in the polarity that gives a positive voltage.

setpoint_amps.description: The current this point was measured at in amperes.

warnings.description: Warnings raised while measuring this point, e.g. a settle timeout.

ColdResistancePointAnalysis.description:
The analysis of one setpoint: exactly the output of
`cold_resistance_point.py`.

current_amps.description: The mean of the two polarities' currents, with the quantisation floor.

offset_voltage_volts.description:
Half the sum of the two polarities' voltages: what didn't reverse with
the current. A diagnostic.

voltage_volts.description:
Half the difference between the two polarities' voltages, so that
anything that doesn't reverse with the current cancels.

warnings.description: Warnings raised by the analysis, e.g. a large offset voltage.

Derived.description:
A value derived by Python from measurements, with its standard uncertainty.

Unlike `Measurement` there are no samples: it's calculated from other
quantities, not sampled.

Measurement.description:
A measured quantity: the samples taken, and the value derived from them.

`value` and `uncertainty` are the mean and standard error returned by
`mean_and_standard_error.py`, not calculated in Rust.

This is the shape every measured field takes, and the unit goes in the name
of the field holding it — `filament_voltage_volts: Measurement` — since the
consumer is another program with no doc comments to read.

samples.description: The individual samples, in the order they were taken.

uncertainty.description: The standard error of the mean.

Polarity.description:
The direction of the current through the filament.

Each side of the filament is switched by one SPDT relay. With both relays
de-energised, both sides sit on the negative rail, no current can flow, and
the current has no direction — that's `Nil`. That is the state the
controller powers up in, and the state cleanup returns to. Energising one
relay or the other puts one side on the positive rail, setting the
direction.

Reversing the direction lets the Seebeck voltages at the filament's
junctions cancel when a forward and a reverse measurement are averaged.

A fourth relay state exists — both energised, both sides on the positive
rail — which is equivalent to `Nil` and is never used.

oneOf.description: Relay 1 energised: current flows through the filament one way.
Both relays de-energised: no current flows, so there is no polarity.
Relay 2 energised: current flows the other way.
